newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Pol Pot said captured by ex-comrades.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Pol Pot said captured by ex-comrades.

text.p: Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot, one of the world's most notorious dictators, has been captured by his former followers who recently broke away from him, the rebels said in a radio broadcast on Friday.
"Pol Pot has been captured," said the radio in a broadcast from the north Cambodian guerrilla zone, monitored in Phnom Penh.
The Khmer Rouge splinter faction said its "national army" had captured Pol Pot on Thursday.
But officials in Phnom Penh were sceptical that the 69-year-old Pol Pot had been captured by renegades from his communist Khmer Rouge army.
"I don't believe it," said a senior official in First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's office.
"There's no news from our people yet and Khmer Rouge radio, at the moment, I don't believe it," Kong Vibol told Reuters.
Khmer Rouge radio reported earlier this week that the despised Pol Pot had turned himself in to them to "confess", but that too was denied by the coalition government in Phnom Penh.
Earlier on Friday Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said the breakaway Khmer Rouge faction was closing in on Pol Pot.
Pol Pot was was holed up in a land-mine strewn mountain camp in northern Cambodia, guarded by his last band of loyal men, the prince said.

Pol Pot, whose 1975-79 Khmer Rouge government was responsible for the death of more than a million Cambodians, has not been seen in public since 1980 two years after his overthrow at the hands of an invading Vietnamese army.
An aide to second prime minister Hun Sen said Pol Pot could not be considered captured until he was in government hands.
"If they say they've captured Pol Pot we can't believe it," said Om Yentieng, an adivser in the second prime minister's office.
"But if they hand him over to the government, for trial in an international court, then it means we've arrested Pol Pot," he said.
The Khmer Rouge has been waging a low-intensity guerrilla war against the government since boycotting a 1993 U.N.-suprevised election.
But the once-formidible Maoist guerrilla army has been decimated in recent years by government offensives, splits and defections.
Pol Pot led the die-hard rump of the Khmer Rouge from its northern stronghold of Anglong Veng until earlier this month when bitter factional erupted, according to reports reaching Phnom Penh.
Government officials say Pol Pot fled from Anglong Veng after ordering the execution of his defence chief and almost a dozen members of his family.
Cambodia's two premiers, who share power in a rocky coalition, were headed for a showdown over policy towards the self-destructing rebel army.
Ranariddh has been negotiating with leaders of the breakaway Khmer Rouge faction with a view to strengthening his political base before electioins, due next year.
Hun Sen decalared such talks illegal and said all Khmer Rouge leaders should be imprisoned. REUTER rsb sc
